audit_notes: Model: pseudo-steady diffusion of mobile species (sol chains or free oil) through the layer, xi = depth/layer_thickness, c(0) = 0 at the wetted surface, c(1) = mobile concentration in the undepleted layer; leaching flux J = (D/L) dc/dxi(0) = D*c/L. Design (bottle-brush matrix, 2 wt% sol, 300 um): J = 1e-15*20/3e-4 = 6.7e-11 kg/(m^2 s) (2.1 g/(m^2 yr)). Baseline (conventional foul-release with 4.5 wt% free oil, 150 um): J = 1e-15*45/1.5e-4 = 3.0e-10 kg/(m^2 s). Expected gain ~78 %. Caveats: (1) same diffusivity for sol oligomers and oil (sol chains of bottle-brush networks are larger and slower, favouring the design); (2) pseudo-steady model of a depleting reservoir, valid for the initial rate; (3) against an oil-free conventional silicone (sol ~3-5 %) the reduction would be smaller; (4) the supersoft design is 300 um thick against 150 um, which halves its flux, a design choice; (5) loss of mobile species is a proxy for stiffening; the link to release performance is not simulated. The fibres do not enter this model. Stress: bottle-brush elastomers have low tear energy (~10-50 J/m^2), a durability concern not covered here. Dimensionless: ratio of mobile concentrations 0.44, thickness ratio 2. Simulation coefficient: design leaching flux 6.7e-11 kg/(m^2 s) (informational).
